feed.title: Online Playgrounds & Compilers — Useful Sites
feed.subtitle: A hand-curated, annotated link directory across ten areas, from software and AI to security, economics and architecture. Every entry states what the resource does and where it parts ways with its neighbours.

entry.title: .NET Fiddle
entry.summary: Write, run and share C# and .NET code in the browser — no install.

entry.title: ES6 Console
entry.summary: A console that compiles modern JavaScript (ES6+) in the browser and shows the result instantly.

entry.title: Liveweave
entry.summary: An in-browser playground to try HTML, CSS and JS with live preview.

entry.title: myCompiler
entry.summary: An online IDE supporting many languages, with no install.

entry.title: Ona (eski Gitpod)
entry.summary: Starting as the Gitpod cloud dev environment, it became Ona in 2025 — a platform for background AI coding agents.

entry.title: OnlineGDB
entry.summary: An online IDE that compiles and debugs C and many languages in the browser (gdb included).

entry.title: Compiler Explorer
entry.summary: Puts the generated assembly beside your source, with optimisation level and compiler version switchable so you see the difference immediately. It moves performance arguments from opinion to measurement.

entry.title: CodePen
entry.summary: A browser playground for HTML, CSS and JavaScript. The real value is discovery — you learn by taking apart other people’s CSS tricks.

entry.title: CoderPad
entry.summary: A collaborative editor for running technical interviews with live coding (many languages).

entry.title: CodeSandbox
entry.summary: Runs projects with full npm dependencies in the browser. Unlike CodePen it opens a real React or Node project as-is.

entry.title: CodeShare
entry.summary: Real-time collaborative code editing in the browser with no install or account — a fast option for remote pairing or an interview.

entry.title: Ideone
entry.summary: Compiles and runs 60+ languages in the browser and accepts an input stream — for trying a language’s syntax without installing anything.

entry.title: JS Bin
entry.summary: A JSFiddle-like scratchpad with a live output panel; showing console output on the same screen is handy when debugging.

entry.title: JSFiddle
entry.summary: The oldest and lightest way to test a small JavaScript snippet — the standard tool for attaching a reproducible example to a bug report.

entry.title: Judge0 IDE
entry.summary: An open-source online compiler whose engine you can self-host — the project people building code assessment systems use as infrastructure.

entry.title: OneLang
entry.summary: An experimental tool that converts code written in one language into others — C#, Java, Python, JavaScript. Against a syntax comparison table it produces working translations, which shows how one language’s idiom lands in another.

entry.title: PlayCode
entry.summary: A JavaScript and TypeScript playground that runs as you type and accepts npm packages. Against CodePen the feedback is instant and the console always visible; against CodeSandbox it is lighter for trying a library.

entry.title: Replit
entry.summary: A collaborative cloud IDE that writes and runs dozens of languages in the browser.

entry.title: RunJS
entry.summary: A JavaScript playground that evaluates as you type, showing a variable’s value without a `console.log`.

entry.title: StackBlitz
entry.summary: Runs Node.js in the browser through WebContainers, so install and restart are instant with no server round trip — it even works offline.

entry.title: Wandbox
entry.summary: Runs dozens of C++ compiler versions side by side — for testing which standard or compiler release a behaviour comes from.
